chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Salih ibn Razin from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman for one thousand dirhams, then sent her to her [family], so she returned herself to him and gifted herself to him, saying: 'I desire you more than I desire this thousand; it is yours.' He accepted it from her, then he divorced her before entering into her. He said: 'She has nothing, and she returns to him five hundred dirhams.'

key_terms.دِرْهَم: A silver coin used as currency in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.عَبْدَ رَبِّهِ: Servant of his Lord (a common epithet/name component)
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if a wife gifts herself back and the husband divorces her before consummation?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the wife’s voluntary gift of herself (hibat al-nafs) is treated as a distinct transaction separate from the dowry, yet the pre-consummation divorce rule still applies to the financial settlement. Consequently, she retains the gifted portion while returning half the original mahr, illustrating the Shia juristic distinction between contractual dowry and voluntary gifts in marital dissolution. This highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh where mutual consent can modify standard inheritance or divorce financial obligations.
